title: Stereotyping (the fallacy)
description: The general beliefs that we use to categorize people, objects, and events while assuming those beliefs are accurate generalizations of the whole group.
logical_form:
All X’s have the property Y (this being a characterization, not a fact).

Z  is an X.

Therefore, Z has the property Y.

examples.example: French people are great at kissing.  Julie is French.  Get me a date!
examples.explanation: “French people are great at kissing” is a stereotype, and believing this to be so is a fallacy.  While it may be the case that *some* or even *most* are great at kissing, we cannot assume this without valid reasons.
This isn’t an argument, but just an assertion, one not even based on any kind of facts.  Stereotypes such as these usually arise from prejudice, ignorance, jealousy, or even hatred.

exceptions: Statistical data can reveal properties of a group that are more common than in other groups, which can affect the probability of any individual member of the group having that property, but we can never assume that all members of the group have that property.
tips: Remember that people are individuals above being members of groups or categories.
references: MAC, M. J. T., PhD, CSAC. (2006). *Critical Thinking for Addiction Professionals*. Springer Publishing Company.
description_et: Üldised uskumused, mida me kasutame inimeste, objektide ja sündmuste kategoriseerimiseks, eeldades samal ajal neid uskumusi, on kogu rühma täpsed üldistused.
logical_form_et:
Kõigil X-del on omadus Y (see on iseloomustus, mitte fakt).

Z on X.

Seetõttu on Z-l omadus Y.
exceptions_et: Statistilised andmed võivad paljastada rühma omadusi, mis on levinumad kui teistes rühmades, mis võivad mõjutada tõenäosust, et rühma mis tahes liikmel on see omadus, kuid me ei saa kunagi eeldada, et see omadus on kõigil rühma liikmetel.
tips_et: Pidage meeles, et inimesed on üksikisikud, mitte rühmade või kategooriate liikmed.

examples_et.example: Prantslased oskavad suurepäraselt suudleda.  Julie on prantslane.  Kutsu mulle kohting!
examples_et.explanation: „Prantsuslased oskavad suurepäraselt suudleda” on stereotüüp ja sellesse uskumine on ekslik.  Kuigi võib juhtuda, et *mõned* või isegi *enamik* oskavad suurepäraselt suudlemist, ei saa me seda eeldada ilma mõjuva põhjuseta.
examples_et.original_example: French people are great at kissing.  Julie is French.  Get me a date!
examples_et.original_explanation: “French people are great at kissing” is a stereotype, and believing this to be so is a fallacy.  While it may be the case that *some* or even *most* are great at kissing, we cannot assume this without valid reasons.
